cells.tense: Right now you hold what your heart knows without rushing it into a choice.
cells.act: stay in the depth of it instead of surfacing
cells.ask: When you feel close to somebody and the truth of it comes quietly, sit there ten minutes before you speak or decide. Don't fix the feeling. Stay under it.
cells.core:
When you feel close to someone, you already do the slower thing — you let what you know sit, and you don't act on it until it has finished being true. Most people mistake that for being slow. It isn't. It's you keeping your whole picture of a person, and your feeling about them, in one hand.

Your gift here is seeing the whole shape of a thing from inside it without losing your footing. The way this grows is depth — going further into a pattern instead of stepping back from it. Read the hard page of a person you love twice, slowly, before you decide anything about them. You'll find they're more like themselves than you thought.
cells.sheetLine: You sit with what you know before moving on it.
cells.verb: Feeling settling into its own depth before it moves
cells.place: Standing outside the whole shape while still held inside it

cells.tense: You're already braced for what the connection is going to mean before it has had a chance.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take one thing that ended this year — a closeness, a habit, a version of someone — and name three things it gave you. Say each one once, plainly. Then close the book on it.
cells.core:
You see whole patterns, and lately you've been finishing them before they arrive — the friendship, the conversation, the version of someone you'll be next month. Your feeling about a person isn't getting time to settle into its own depth; you're reading the ending off the first page. That readiness is your own care, turned up. It isn't a flaw.

What brings you back is gathering what change actually grew, instead of predicting it. Look at one connection that has already shifted and count what it gave you. Not what you lost — what you got. Patient waiting has been rewarded before and will be again, but only when you let it arrive unbeaten by you.

cells.tense: You used to be able to sit with what you knew, and that door is behind you.
cells.act: reconcile what you know with what you feel about it
cells.ask: Think of one person you feel tangled about. Put two lines on a page — what you know to be true, and what you actually feel. No fixing. Just both.
cells.core:
Seeing the whole shape got harder to reach. Something got pulled out from under it, and this place has been quieter since. What you know is still in you. It just isn't arriving. You notice you can't hold a whole picture of someone anymore, only fragments, and the fragments don't line up.

The way through is to gather your thinking into one line instead of forcing feeling back into a place that's empty. Put what you know and what you feel about one person side by side on a page. You aren't trying to make them agree. You're giving the two halves of you somewhere to stand next to each other, where neither has to win.

cells.tense: The pattern gets seen and said by you, and you don't put your name on it.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: When someone tells you something that matters, hold it one question longer than you normally would. Don't wrap it up. Then note, privately, whose eyes caught the shape.
cells.core:
You see the whole shape of things between people. You say it like it came from nowhere, in a voice with no author in it. Nobody around you believes that voice — they've watched it happen too often. The shape you find is holding several conversations up, and your account has you finding nothing.

Mark it as yours. Not announced — just carried. When a pattern shows itself to you about someone close, stay in it one beat longer than is polite, and let yourself know you caught it. You don't have to present the finding to be the one who found it.
